description:
After commit 4428dbd 'extract MemoryBackend to feature-gated src/memory', the layout is:

- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs     (2742 lines, the actual MemoryBackend code)
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/seed.rs (821 lines, the seed-data fixture)

Rust supports this (the Rust 2018 path resolution rules allow either 'memory.rs + memory/' or 'memory/mod.rs + memory/'), but it is the less-common shape. The conventional layout when a module grows submodules is to move the parent file from src/memory.rs to src/memory/mod.rs so all related code sits in the same directory.

A new contributor opening 'crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/' in their editor will see only seed.rs and miss the 2742-line parent. The crate's own AGENTS.md and README don't document this layout choice, so the discoverability cost is real.

Either convention works; pick one and apply it consistently. The other extension-server crates in the workspace (per the cookie-cutter rule) should match: if any of them have their MemoryBackend in 'src/memory/mod.rs', mail-server should too; if all of them use 'src/memory.rs + src/memory/seed.rs', that becomes the canonical pattern and the four-line note belongs in workspace AGENTS.md.

Verification needed: spot-check the other 7 *-server crates with memory modules to see what they do, then commit to one layout and propagate.
title: memory.rs lives at src/memory.rs with sibling src/memory/seed.rs
